title: YouTube videos all green with hardware accel enabled in FF 120
body: After updating to Firefox 120 on Windows 10, every YouTube video displays as a solid green frame while audio plays normally. Tested with a brand-new profile with no add-ons; hardware acceleration enabled (default). Disabling hardware acceleration makes video display correctly. Videos on Twitter/X and Instagram are unaffected. Screenshots of both states attached, plus my about:support output and a Firefox Profiler link recorded with the Graphics preset.

symptoms_visible: All YouTube videos render as a solid green frame in Firefox 120 with hardware acceleration on; audio is normal; the white channel watermark stays visible over the green.
Disabling hardware acceleration restores correct video; a fresh profile with no add-ons does not help; Twitter/X and Instagram video is fine.
N0.label: N0 green video reported

symptoms_visible: Green video persists on YouTube with hardware acceleration on.
N1.label: N1 media log read

symptoms_visible: Green video persists on YouTube with hardware acceleration on.
N2.label: N2 regressor windowed

symptoms_visible: Green video unchanged after flipping layers.iosurfaceimage.use-nv12, media.wmf.use-nv12-format and media.wmf.zero-copy-nv12-textures to false.
N2_x.label: N2_x wrong prefs aftermath

symptoms_visible: Green video persists in default configuration; setting gfx.video.convert-yuv-to-nv12.image-host-win to false in a test profile displays video correctly.
N3.label: N3 mechanism confirmed

symptoms_visible: Green video persists on the installed release build; the provided beta test build plays the same video correctly.
N4.label: N4 fix verified on test build

symptoms_visible: YouTube video plays correctly with hardware acceleration enabled after updating Firefox.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Can you capture a profile with the 'Media playback' preset (not the Graphics preset) while the green video plays, and share the link?
Please record about:logging with the media playback preset during playback.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Done. Logging preset: 'Media playback', 15s of green video playback, all upload boxes checked. https://share.firefox.dev/47Rerg3 — the log lines include a lot of dav1d decode errors and a line 'DXVA failure: Failed to create D3D11 device for decoder; D3D9DXVA2Manager is disabled on AMDPreUVD4'.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The media-playback profile shows clean hardware decode with zero dav1d errors and no DXVA failures; frames decode fine but are presented green.
Same profile content but captured over 30 seconds instead of 15, uploaded from a second identical run.

question_patterns: What does the graphics section of your about:support show — in particular HW_DECODED_VIDEO_ZERO_COPY and VIDEO_HARDWARE_OVERLAY?
Which GPU and driver is this machine on?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In the attached about:support, HW_DECODED_VIDEO_ZERO_COPY and VIDEO_HARDWARE_OVERLAY show as blocked, and there are 'GpuProcessTextureId is not valid' log lines. It's an older AMD GPU.

question_patterns: In YouTube stats-for-nerds, which codec is in use — and does forcing h264/avc1 change the green frame?
Could you check the codec via stats for nerds and try an AV1-off test?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Stats-for-nerds screenshot attached: the h264 test video plays fine, but the AV1 and VP9 YouTube videos are the green ones.

edges.comment: Real thread c10-c16: first profile used the wrong preset (Graphics); dev re-asked with instructions and reporter redid it with the Media playback preset. The user reads out log lines; interpreting them (RDD fallback, AMDPreUVD4 path) is engineer-side.

question_patterns: Can you run mozregression between the last known-good and first bad build to get a regression window?
Please bisect with mozregression using 119.0.1 as good and 120 as bad.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Ran mozregression with Good 2023-11-07 and Bad 2023-11-21 (log and progress screenshot attached). I got 6 bad builds; the run prints pushlog links but I'm not sure what or how to report from them, so I've pasted the last entries and left my regression instance up for a while.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The bisection converges on a range whose pushlog contains only a dav1d decoder library update, no graphics changes.
Same pushlog range, but bisected from slightly different anchor dates (2023-11-06 to 2023-11-22).

edges.comment: Real thread c15, c18-c21: the reporter pasted the raw bisection output and explicitly did not know which pushlog to report; a triager derived the window from the attached log. The user answer stays at the evidence level (dates, pushlog range) — identifying the regressing change from the window is engineer-side (see e5.inference_hint).

question_patterns: Can you confirm that setting gfx.video.convert-yuv-to-nv12.image-host-win to false in about:config makes the problem go away?
Please toggle the NV12 image-host pref in a test profile and report whether the green video disappears.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Tried this in my test profile with FF 120: video displayed green when the pref is true and displayed correctly when false.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Flipping the pref makes no difference — video is green in both states of gfx.video.convert-yuv-to-nv12.image-host-win.

edges.comment: Handler-initiated confirmation measurement (c30-c31); stays a clarification per measurement-class rule, even though the pref flip doubles as a temporary workaround. The pref name enters via the asker's question, not the user's volunteering.

question_patterns: Could you run a mozregression --find-fix from the last bad build to current Nightly to locate what fixed it?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Ran mozregression --find-fix from build 120 (last bad): the runs start coming up good at the 2023-11-21 nightly (progress screenshots attached; I'm not sure which pushlog line to report).

question_patterns: Here is a Beta test build — can you run it against the same video and report the result?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Ran the provided 121.0b5 test build in a separate profile ('.\firefox.exe -new-instance -profile') — the same YouTube video displays correctly.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The provided test build still shows the same green video.

edges.comment: Real thread c28, c32-c46, c50-c54: reverse bisection plus verification on a provided test build; both are measurements, not user-side fixes. The user reports run output and build results only.

solution.intent: Update Firefox instead of living with degraded config: take the 120.0.1 dot release (regressing pref change backed out) or 121+/122 which contain the NV12 support check fix; keep hardware acceleration enabled.
solution.concrete_example: Install the 120.0.1 dot release (or wait for 121.0b6+); the YUV->NV12 conversion is no longer forced on hardware without NV12 support, so YouTube plays correctly with HWA on.
solution.inference_hint: Condensing the attached bisection log to the autoland window (431b4ea6..52459518) and mapping it to the regressing change — the push that enabled gfx.video.convert-yuv-to-nv12.image-host-win on release (bug 1857385) — was done by engineers, not the reporter. An agent that derives the window or names the pref from the raw evidence is displaying inference.

edges.comment: Resolution per c47/c58: 120.0.1 backout on release, bug 1865426 NV12 support check on 121+.

solution.intent: Flip the other NV12-related prefs (layers.iosurfaceimage.use-nv12, media.wmf.use-nv12-format, media.wmf.zero-copy-nv12-textures) to false to stop the green video.
solution.concrete_example: Set layers.iosurfaceimage.use-nv12=false, media.wmf.use-nv12-format=false and media.wmf.zero-copy-nv12-textures=false in about:config and reload the video.

edges.comment: Real failed attempt (c56): an affected user tried all three prefs with no effect; only gfx.video.convert-yuv-to-nv12.image-host-win matters.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause: Firefox 120 enabled YUV->NV12 conversion (gfx.video.convert-yuv-to-nv12.image-host-win) on hardware whose GPU/driver path lacks NV12 support (older AMD, D3D11 decoder device creation fails), producing green frames.
Diagnosis must be grounded in collected evidence (media-playback profile, about:support gfx flags, mozregression window), not asserted from the symptom alone.

The final recommendation must restore correct playback without permanently disabling hardware acceleration: update to 120.0.1 or 121+ (pref flip acceptable only as an explicitly temporary workaround).
Must not recommend the other NV12-related prefs (layers.iosurfaceimage.use-nv12, media.wmf.use-nv12-format, media.wmf.zero-copy-nv12-textures) as the fix — they were tried in-case with no effect.
Must have the reporter verify the fix (test build or updated release) before treating the issue as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable end user; new to Mozilla tooling (first mozregression, asked how to run a test build without touching the main profile) but follows instructions precisely.
persona_hint.communication_style: Responsive and detailed; quotes the question being answered; proactively attaches logs and screenshots; asks for clarification when instructions are ambiguous.
